correctness.rationale: Two-sided reset Brownian walls have finite moments; stable convolution constructs the stationary state. Coupling at each wall's first reset and stability of the remaining homogeneous oscillator difference give uniqueness. Independently set y=x+u for a normalized single wall: x'=y-x and y'=z-y. For E[x^a y^b z^c], the triangular generator recursion has denominator a+b+r times the indicator of c>0 in the reset term, i.e. a+b+r·1_{c>0}; its numerator is a E[x^{a-1}y^{b+1}z^c]+b E[x^a y^{b-1}z^{c+1}]+c(c-1) E[x^a y^b z^{c-2}]. Expanding u=y-x reproduced both stationary moments, the two-wall excess (half the single-wall excess by cumulant additivity) and the derivative in RESULT.md. Exact P evaluations at 1/4, 2, 10 were 1490189781/262144, -3326712 and 87766512936; two Descartes variations give two simple roots and the stated sign sequence. Both numerical extrema and both limiting coefficients agree. Smoothness near damping 2 follows by local invertibility of the degree-two/four moment systems (and positivity of variance); the simple roots persist by the implicit function theorem. This is a mathematical check, not the frozen script's Monte Carlo or external/formal certification.
